extracted.intended_audience: journalists, journalism educators, news managers, health professionals and organisations concerned with trauma-aware reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practices for reporting on violence, crisis and tragedy that protect victims and support journalists' psychological resilience. Emphasises ethical reporting, evidence-based trauma science, newsroom duty of care, and professional exchange/training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compassionate, ethical and professional reporting on victims and survivors
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocates for compassionate, ethical and professional reporting on victims and survivors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Global Center emphasises reporting that treats victims and survivors with sensitivity, dignity and respect (e.g., its antecedent programs 'assist[ed] journalism students in reporting on victims of violence with sensitivity, dignity and respect'). Implicitly this calls for avoiding sensationalism or practices that retraumatize or dehumanize people affected by violence or tragedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma-aware reporting: knowledge, skills and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides reporters and filmmakers with the knowledge, skills and support necessary to meet the challenge of trauma-aware reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical capacity-building for journalists and filmmakers — training, resources and supports — is a core standard so reporters can cover trauma, conflict and tragedy responsibly and effectively across media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounding practices in evidence-based trauma science and high journalism standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounded in both the highest standards of journalism practice and evidence-based trauma science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting practices and newsroom supports should be informed by empirical research on trauma and by accepted professional journalism standards; research and clinical evidence should shape guidance to reduce harm to sources and to journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance press freedom through research and education on trauma-facing reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Advances press freedom through research and education on the impact of trauma-facing reporting and best practices to foster resilience in news professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion links protecting journalists' ability to report freely with providing research-informed education on how trauma-reporting affects journalists and communities, and with developing best practices that support both reporting quality and reporter wellbeing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster best practices in professional trauma awareness and duty of care
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides a professional forum ... and foster best practices in professional trauma awareness and duty of care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisations and newsrooms are expected to adopt a duty-of-care approach: implementing trauma awareness, policies and practices that protect staff (e.g., managerial training, peer support, institutional supports). The Global Center promotes establishing and sharing such best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote psychological resilience of journalists worldwide
rubrics_metrics.description: Dedicated to ... the psychological resilience of journalists worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports and initiatives should aim to strengthen journalists' mental health and resilience through training, peer support, access to clinical expertise, and organisational practices that recognise the emotional impact of trauma-facing reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide professional forums for sharing knowledge and strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides a professional forum for journalists across all media to share knowledge and ideas, advance strategies related to effective, ethical reporting on violence and tragedy and foster best practices in professional trauma awareness and duty of care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable implementation includes convenings, forums, fellowships, workshops and exchanges where journalists, clinicians and researchers collaborate to develop and disseminate ethical, trauma-aware reporting strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training, fellowship and peer-support program examples as implementation norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically: hosted journalist and documentary film fellows; trained journalists and managers; sponsored workshops and public programs; pioneered newsroom peer support programs; nurtured academic studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These activities are presented as concrete, normative examples of how to implement the Center's standards: fellowships, newsroom training for managers and reporters, workshops on specific issues (mass shootings, forced migration, etc.), peer-support programs and research partnerships.
